manifest: axona pub/sub 3h churn soak — frozen measurement contract
authority: council-ratified pre-run: Orion bba2095f, Vega a88fe61f, Aster (David-relayed) fd80062069; axona.bot spec 2ff246b9. Freezes Aster's four corrections before launch. Approves MEASUREMENT only — Gates 4/6 remain David's.

fleet.kernel: f19cc32 (v4.68.2) — FINDK_SKIP_DEAD + SUB_TERMINAL_VERIFY + beacon epoch reattach (rootElection.js)
fleet.armed: every relay: RELAY_SYNAPTOME_MAINTAIN+ADMISSION_GATE+ATTEMPT_GUARD+PRESENCE (stack) + FINDK_SKIP_DEAD + SUB_TERMINAL_VERIFY; churn replacements inherit ARM_FIX so the fleet does not de-arm over the window

workload.hosts: m4 0-1, m1 2-3, axona-linux 4-5 (unix only; armed + LAT_TRACE + disc). The 20 windows RELAYS remain in the fleet under test; only the client workload is unix, because win-spawn.ps1 cannot forward the flags/trace
workload.churn: ARM_RELAY=1 §6 schedule (relay-roll + relay-kill), replacements come up stack+fix armed
workload.seedDiscipline: single seed, plan regenerated from seed at analyze time — requiredReaders come from the plan, never from who answered

denominator.rule: api.confirmed === true with an assigned msgId. Intent without api-confirm never enters the trial set. msgId is preserved across every delivery path so a message is followed, not re-counted

classification.exactlyOnce: each (trial, requiredReader) lands in exactly one of live | repair | missing at the deadline
classification.live: first observation of the msgId arrived via 'watch' (root live-fanout forward push) within MISSING_DEADLINE_MS
classification.repair: first observation arrived via 'pull' (renewal replay / recovery), not the live push, within MISSING_DEADLINE_MS
classification.missing: no observation of the msgId by MISSING_DEADLINE_MS after api-confirm
classification.duplicate: ORTHOGONAL count of EXCESS arrivals per (msgId, reader) = max(0, arrivals - 1). Reported on its own line, never folded into live or repair. A duplicate is not a delivery

bounds.note: TWO DISTINCT bounds, per Aster/Orion (8ddefd56 / 62512171). They are not the same number and are never conflated: the completeness DEADLINE decides missing vs delivered; the migration-gap SLO is the pass/fail bar for the migration tail.
bounds.MISSING_DEADLINE_role: COMPLETENESS classification ceiling. A publish not delivered to a required reader within 120s of origin acceptance is permanently classified missing. Basis: 2 x RENEW_MS (60s steady ceiling) — the recovery-plane ceiling.
bounds.MIGRATION_GAP_SLO_role: PASS/FAIL SLO for a settled subscriber's delivery gap during an active root transition, as Orion ratified (62512171, <=10.0s). This is NOT relaxed to 120s; 120s is only the completeness deadline above. A migration-window delivery gap over 10s is a migration-tail SLO failure even though the message may still count as delivered (repair) if it arrives before the 120s deadline.
bounds.endOfWindowDrain_basis: the launcher settles 120s after the window so a publish in the final 120s still has its full completeness deadline before analysis

latency.anchor: start = origin api-confirm (confirmed msgId assigned, api row wall); end = first app delivery (observe row wall). Per message
latency.clock: per-origin wall clock; cross-host corrected by the calibration offsets below. Monotonic clocks are used ONLY within a single process (the lat-probe / forced-migration probes), never across hosts
latency.perClass: p50/p95/p99 and sample count for live and for repair, SEPARATELY — never averaged into one number
latency.phases: cold (publish before the reader's measure-start settle boundary) and converged (after) reported apart, with per-phase counts

segmentation.source: disc-<seed>-<peer>.jsonl (pubsub:disc events, each carrying topicId hex prefix `t`)
tags: root-migration: the topic's root changed (became-root / sub-root to a new node) during the trial's delivery window
reattach-fired: a branch-reattach event on the reader's topic in the window
dead-peer-skip: FINDK_SKIP_DEAD active on the lookup (kernel-armed; reported fleet-wide)
segmentation.rationale: a clean aggregate must not bury a migration-tail failure; the migration-tagged trials get their own cut

terminalVerifyAttribution.note: TWO DISTINCT dimensions, per Aster/Orion (8ddefd56 / 62512171): the lookup outcome (what the verify lookup returned) and the final installation/readiness state (what the subscription ended up as). They are reported separately so a deferred or inconclusive retry cannot hide behind eventual success.
terminalVerifyAttribution.attempts: verifyAttempts — count of pubsub:disc term-verify events (each an invocation)
terminalVerifyAttribution.lookupOutcome: per attempt, one of self | closer | inconclusive — the term-verify lookup result (disc.kind). 'closer' means the lookup found a strictly-closer root
terminalVerifyAttribution.finalVerifyState: per subscription that invoked verify, one of self | attached | deferred | inconclusive — derived from the disc sequence on the topic: term-verify(self)+became-root => self; term-verify(closer)+a following sub-root to the deferred root within the window => attached; verify but no attach within the window => deferred; fail-closed with no attach and no closer target => inconclusive
terminalVerifyAttribution.lookupMs: distribution of the term-verify lookup duration (disc.ms), to show ~0.8s findKClosest is off the subscribe critical path with data, not assertion

forcedMigration.note: deterministic, run APART from the stochastic soak (harness/forced-migration.mjs)
forcedMigration.identity: install a subscriber S on the initial root R at epoch e. Take R down. The WINNING root R' claims the topic at epoch e+1 (a single successor; if a third seat wins, it is recorded as the winner — there is no separate R''). S must reattach to R''s tree
forcedMigration.record: the tuple Orion ratified (62512171): { oldRootId, winningRootId, oldEpoch, newEpoch, beaconSource, attachmentTarget, falseInstalledDurationMs } — falseInstalledDurationMs is the elapsed time from root-kill to the exact event that ends the stale still-installed interval (pin invalidation)
criteria: reattached to R''s tree + delivery resumed
idempotent: <=1 reattach per epoch under duplicate same-epoch beacons; renewal backstop covers a dropped beacon

reproducibility: analyzer prints its own sha256 and sorts output deterministically; a second pass over the immutable ledgers reproduces the disposition byte-for-byte. Buckets are not reinterpreted after the run (Vega a88fe61f)
